walkthroughs.body_html:
Depth Study: Germany 1918-45 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Depth Study: Germany 1918-45 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Depth Study: Germany 1918-45.

mcqs.q: Which Article of Versailles forced Germany to accept war guilt?
options: Article 48
Article 231
Article 14
Article 5

mcqs.q: What ended the period of Weimar stability?
options: Munich Putsch
Reichstag Fire
Wall Street Crash 1929
Hyperinflation

mcqs.q: Why was the Berlin Wall built in 1961?
options: The Berlin Wall was built to stop a Western invasion of East Berlin.
The Berlin Wall was built by NATO to keep East Germans out of West Germany.
To stop the mass flow of East Germans to the West via Berlin (millions had fled), which was draining the GDR of skilled workers and threatening the regime's survival.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.

mcqs.q: Why did the Treaty of Versailles cause resentment in Germany?
options: Because Germany lost more soldiers than any other country in the war.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.
It assigned sole war guilt to Germany (Article 231) and imposed harsh reparations, territorial losses and military restrictions.
The Berlin Wall was built by NATO to keep East Germans out of West Germany.

mcqs.q: How did Hitler come to power in 1933?
options: Hitler seized power through a violent coup or revolution.
He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg as part of a conservative political deal, after the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
The Berlin Wall was built by NATO to keep East Germans out of West Germany.
